title: Mortgage Calculation Methodology
overview: Mortgage calculations determine monthly payments based on loan principal, interest rate, and term. Understanding PMT formula, amortization, and total interest helps borrowers make informed decisions.

methods.name: PMT Formula (Standard Amortization)
methods.description: The standard formula for calculating fixed monthly payments on a fully amortizing loan. This is used by virtually all lenders.
limitations: Does not include property taxes and insurance (escrow)
Does not account for PMI (private mortgage insurance)

methods.name: PITI (Full Housing Payment)
methods.description: Complete monthly housing cost including Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance. This represents the true monthly obligation.

formula.name: PITI Calculation
formula.expression: PITI = P&I + Taxes/12 + Insurance/12 + PMI (if applicable)

variables.meaning: Principal and Interest from PMT formula
Private mortgage insurance if down payment < 20%

methods.name: APR vs APY Understanding
methods.description: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) includes fees, while APY (Annual Percentage Yield) accounts for compounding. For mortgages, APR is the regulated disclosure rate.

formula.name: APR Calculation
formula.description: APR includes points, origination fees, and other costs spread over loan term

limitations: Different lenders may include different fees
Assumes loan is held full term

sources.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau - Mortgage Guide

footnotes: 28% rule: Housing should be ≤28% of gross monthly income
36% rule: Total debt should be ≤36% of gross monthly income
Total interest paid often exceeds original loan amount on 30-year mortgages
Biweekly payments can save years of interest and thousands of dollars
disclaimer: Mortgage calculations are estimates. Actual payments depend on your credit score, down payment, and lender terms. Always get official loan estimates from lenders.
